title: The Garden of Rosewater Lane
premise: Wendell Galloway has spent a decade hiding behind the counter of his bookshop on Rosewater Lane, raising his daughter alone after the scandal that ended his engagement to estate heiress Marguerite Voss. When a freak snowstorm traps them both in the shop overnight alongside her brother Julian—Marguerite's rival for their grandmother's contested inheritance—the three are forced to confront the betrayal that shattered them all. As the town's winter festival approaches, Wendell must choose between the safety of invisibility and claiming both the woman he loves and the standing in the community he forfeited, while Marguerite learns that winning the inheritance means nothing if she keeps losing herself.
about_author: Bram Iversen is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent fifteen years watching love stories unfold between the shelves before writing his own. He lives in a converted carriage house with too many first editions and a garden he insists on calling wild rather than neglected.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ten years of careful routine: opening the bookshop, school runs with daughter Poppy, avoiding the Voss family estate at all costs. A letter arrives announcing the reading of Grandmother Voss's will—and naming Wendell's shop as part of the disputed property. Emotional beat: dread cracking open an ordered life.

chapters.title: Marguerite Returns
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She comes to Rosewater Lane to survey the property before the will reading, armed with lawyers and armor. Seeing Wendell across the counter unearths the mistake of their twenties she's never confessed. Emotional beat: longing sharpened into hostility; she leaves without buying anything.

chapters.title: Julian's Gambit
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The charming younger Voss arrives in town, befriending Poppy at the bookshop while quietly gathering evidence that the will favors him. He engineers a meeting between all three parties at the shop on the eve of the reading. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon; the reader sees his calculation beneath the warmth.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The storm hits early; roads close; the three are trapped in the bookshop overnight with candles, wine, and ten years of unfinished sentences. Old wounds surface—what really happened the night the engagement collapsed. Emotional beat: forced intimacy dissolving defenses, then re-arming them by dawn.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Said
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Confined another day, she admits to Wendell that she let him take the blame publicly to protect her family's name—a survival choice that cost them everything. He refuses absolution. Emotional beat: confession without forgiveness; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Poppy's Question
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Roads clear but the will reading looms. Poppy, having grown attached to both visitors, asks why her father never talks about the Vosses—or her other parent. Wendell realizes his invisibility has become its own cage, teaching his daughter to hide too. Emotional beat: grief turning toward resolve.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The will reveals Grandmother left the disputed parcel to whoever can prove they'll steward it—not inherit it—for the town's good, with the festival as the deadline for public claims. Julian produces documents implicating Wendell in the old scandal; Marguerite stays silent. Emotional beat: betrayal repeated; power corrupting even grief.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating Wendell and Marguerite. On the eve of the lantern festival, each confronts the person in the mirror: Wendell drafts a public claim telling the whole truth about the scandal, including his own complicity; Marguerite decides to testify against Julian despite the cost to her name. Emotional beat: forgiveness of self preceding forgiveness of each other.

chapters.title: Lanterns Over Rosewater Lane
chapters.summary: Climax, all three POVs converging. At the festival, Julian's forged evidence collapses when Marguerite speaks; Wendell tells the crowd the full story, asking not for pity but for the chance to keep the shop as a commons. The town votes with raised lanterns. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation; power reclaimed through vulnerability.

chapters.title: Spring on Rosewater Lane
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. Months later: the bookshop hosts the town's first community reading series, Julian departs diminished but honest, and Marguerite stays—not as an heiress reclaiming ground, but as a partner rebuilding it. Poppy plants roses out front. Emotional beat: quiet earned joy; inheritance redefined as what we choose to tend.
